squawks.headline: Fed's Williams says inflation is stubbornly high but the situation does not call for dramatic policy action
squawks.detail: New York Fed President Williams said shocks from tariffs and energy are still feeding into inflation readings, with signs of spillover into broader inflation data. He described the economy as resilient and the labour market as solid.

squawks.headline: US official says fighter jets hit an IRGC missile launch site on Qeshm Island in self-defence
squawks.detail: A US military official said US fighter aircraft struck an IRGC missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island. A US official told Axios the strike was self-defence after Iran targeted US personnel and assets.

squawks.headline: Fed's Williams says the US economy is strong and getting stronger, and inflation is not moving in the right direction
squawks.detail: New York Fed President Williams said the Fed still has more work to do to bring inflation back to 2%.

squawks.headline: Iran says it is seriously pursuing a diplomatic way out of the impasse, ISNA reports
squawks.detail: Iran's ISNA news agency reports that Tehran is seriously pursuing a diplomatic end to the impasse. The report follows US strikes on Qeshm Island and tanker incidents in the Strait of Hormuz earlier today.

squawks.headline: Zelenskiy says Ukraine's security service carried out the attack on the Crimea bridge
squawks.detail: Ukrainian President Zelenskiy said the Security Service of Ukraine and other services carried out the attack, which he said hit a key Russian military supply route in the south with missiles and drones. He said Ukraine had long warned Russia over its attacks on bridges, cities and energy infrastructure.

squawks.headline: German Defence Minister Pistorius rejects criticism of Ukraine's deep strikes on Russian military targets
squawks.detail: Germany's defence minister said strikes on non-civilian targets in Russia should be seen as legal and legitimate, and called criticism of them foolish. He said Russia's daily attacks on Ukraine's energy, water and heating infrastructure should be condemned instead.

squawks.headline: NATO's Rutte backs Ukraine's deep strikes, saying Russia's war machine must be disabled
squawks.detail: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte backed Ukraine's deep strikes on Russia, saying it is important to disable Russia's war machine. His remarks came after a senior US official criticised the strikes for risking escalation.

squawks.headline: Houthis say they attacked two sections of Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline with drones
squawks.detail: In two statements, Yemen's Houthis said they used two drones against the pipeline in the Riyadh area and then three more against another section. No damage, disruption to supply or market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: US Democratic senator files bill to revoke China's normal trade status before Trump-Xi meeting
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that US Senator Tammy Baldwin introduced legislation on Tuesday to remove China's normal trade status and favourable tariff treatment. The bill comes days before President Trump and President Xi meet for the third time this year to discuss their trade truce.

squawks.headline: Fed Governor Cook refuses to attend the hearing convened by Trump, citing the Fed's independence
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that Fed Governor Lisa Cook will not attend the hearing called by President Trump. She said taking part in proceedings she considers unfair would put at risk the central bank's unique status and independence.

squawks.headline: Iran's foreign minister says regional security should be built by regional states without foreign interference
squawks.detail: Iranian reports cite Foreign Minister Araghchi as saying all countries in the region believe security should come from within the region, without outside interference. The remarks follow reported US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island.

squawks.headline: UK PM Burnham says some of Milburn's reforms will be dealt with in the Budget
squawks.detail: Prime Minister Burnham said some of Alan Milburn's welfare and youth employment reforms are for the Budget, Sky News reported.

squawks.headline: Welsh government's first multiyear Budget puts over £1.5bn of capital spending into social homes over three years
squawks.detail: Inside Housing reports that the Plaid Cymru-led Welsh government's first full Budget sets aside more than £1.5bn over three years towards its target of 20,000 homes.

squawks.headline: UK PM Burnham says an EU deal could lower power and grocery costs
squawks.detail: Prime Minister Burnham said a deal with the EU could reduce the cost of electricity and groceries. He made the remark as he set out the government's position on the UK's future relationship with the EU.

squawks.headline: UK PM Burnham says there is no rush to settle long-term EU relationship and next steps will come later this year
squawks.detail: Prime Minister Burnham said there was no hurry to decide the UK's long-term relationship with the EU. He said the government would set out its next steps on that relationship later this year.

squawks.headline: Senior US official criticises Ukraine's deep strikes on Russia, citing risk of escalation
squawks.detail: A senior US official criticised Ukraine's long-range strikes inside Russia and pointed to the risk of escalation, according to a market news report. The report did not name the official and no market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Iran's foreign minister calls for continued regional consultations after talks with Qatari delegation in Muscat
squawks.detail: Iranian state news agency reports Foreign Minister Araghchi met a Qatari delegation in Oman's capital and stressed the need for ongoing consultations among countries in the region. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Iran's foreign minister rejects media reports of an Iranian plot to use chemical weapons in Washington
squawks.detail: Iran's foreign minister dismissed reports from the past 72 hours that Iran planned a chemical weapons attack in Washington and was building missile bases under dams. He compared them to propaganda before the Iraq war and said Israel was behind them.

squawks.headline: An official confirms the US has attacked Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz
squawks.detail: An official confirmed the US attack on Qeshm Island. Earlier reports of the strike were unconfirmed or came from Iranian media.

squawks.headline: Fed's Hammack says inflation is moving the wrong way and housing is the only sector where she sees rates restricting activity
squawks.detail: Cleveland Fed President Hammack said yields are being pushed up by expectations for growth and for the Fed, and that inflation is heading in the wrong direction. She also said housing is the one part of the economy where she sees rates holding activity back.

squawks.headline: Atlanta Fed interim President Venable says inflation is still too high and the job market is stable
squawks.detail: Venable, interim president of the Atlanta Fed, commented on inflation and the labour market on 17 November. Posts in the batch report no figures and no market reaction.

squawks.headline: Fed's Hammack says intervening in markets is harder during a tightening cycle
squawks.detail: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said market intervention is more difficult while policy is being tightened. She made the remarks during her earlier comments on Fed and Treasury coordination in market stress.

squawks.headline: Iran's IRGC navy says a fourth tanker has caught fire in the eastern Strait of Hormuz
squawks.detail: Fars News, citing the IRGC navy, reported that a fourth tanker caught fire in the east of the Strait of Hormuz in recent hours. Iran had earlier reported that a third tanker hit a sea mine there.

squawks.headline: US NAHB housing market index falls to 25 in November against 29 forecast; business inventories rise 0.5% m/m
squawks.detail: The NAHB homebuilder sentiment index fell to 25 in November, from 29 the previous month and below the 29 forecast. US business inventories rose 0.5% m/m, in line with forecast, after 0.4% previously.

squawks.headline: Fed's Hammack says Fed and Treasury can coordinate on market stress and Fed is better placed to act in extreme dislocation
squawks.detail: Cleveland Fed President Hammack said the Fed and Treasury can work together during market stress while the Fed keeps its independence on monetary policy. She also said the Fed is now better positioned to act when markets are severely dislocated.

squawks.headline: Fed's Hammack says her views on monetary tightening are unchanged since yesterday
squawks.detail: Cleveland Fed President Hammack said her views on tightening monetary policy have not changed since yesterday. She also said the US Treasury and the Fed have different objectives in the bond market.

squawks.headline: France rejects Russia's claim that French troops are taking part in the Ukraine war, calling it absurd
squawks.detail: France dismissed the Russian claim that French forces are involved in the war in Ukraine. Earlier, Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov said Moscow would treat French troops deployed in Ukraine as direct participation in the war.

squawks.headline: Fed's Hammack says the Fed should agree principles for Treasury market interventions in advance, while markets are calm
squawks.detail: Cleveland Fed President Hammack told a Brookings Institution event that any interventions should be temporary and targeted, with an exit strategy and timely sale of holdings once stability returns, and that she supports enhancements to the standing repo facility. Her prepared remarks did not address the economic or monetary policy outlook.

squawks.headline: Hungary's central bank leaves interest rates unchanged after a split vote, Governor Varga says
squawks.detail: Hungarian central bank governor Varga said policymakers decided to keep rates on hold and that the vote was divided. The post gave no rate level or vote breakdown.

squawks.headline: US October capacity utilisation slips to 76.4%, below 76.8% forecast; manufacturing output rises 0.3% m/m
squawks.detail: Figures from the US October industrial production report show capacity utilisation at 76.4%, down from 76.9% previously. Manufacturing output rose 0.3% m/m against a 0.2% forecast, and industrial production growth eased to 2.1% y/y from 2.25%.

squawks.headline: US industrial production falls 0.4% m/m in October, against 0.1% rise forecast; previous month 0.7%
squawks.detail: US industrial production fell 0.4% month on month, compared with a forecast of a 0.1% rise and 0.7% growth in the previous month.

squawks.headline: Fed's Waller says the Fed will back responsible payments innovation and makes no comment on monetary policy
squawks.detail: Fed Governor Waller said the Fed will support innovation in payment systems, which he described as still at an early stage, and said traditional money and payment systems still play a key role. He did not comment on monetary policy or the economic outlook.

squawks.headline: Lawyer for Fed Governor Cook threatens to stay away from White House mortgage fraud hearing next month
squawks.detail: In a letter seen by Reuters on Tuesday, a lawyer for Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook called the planned White House hearing into mortgage fraud allegations unfair. The letter says Cook has no legal obligation to take part.

squawks.headline: Iran's Sepah News reports US air strikes on Qeshm Island, following earlier unconfirmed reports
squawks.detail: Iran's Sepah News reports US air strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island. Earlier reports of the strike had been unconfirmed. The posts report no market reaction.

squawks.headline: Iran's navy says a third tanker has hit a sea mine and caught fire in the eastern Strait of Hormuz
squawks.detail: Iranian state news agency IRNA, citing Iran's navy, reported a third tanker struck a naval mine and caught fire east of Hormuz. Earlier, Iranian state media reported that a liquefied gas carrier and an oil tanker had hit mines in the strait.

squawks.headline: US Treasury yields climb after US data; 10-year up 1.82bp at 5.139%, 2-year up 2.39bp at 4.851%
squawks.detail: US Treasury yields rose after the release of US economic data. The 10-year note was last up 1.82bp at 5.139% and the 2-year was up 2.39bp at 4.851%.

squawks.headline: Unconfirmed reports say the US has struck Iran's Qeshm Island after an Iranian attack in Bahrain earlier today
squawks.detail: Israel's N12 News cites unofficial sources linked to Iran as reporting US attacks on Qeshm Island. The reports describe the strikes as a response to an Iranian attack in Bahrain on Tuesday morning; there is no official confirmation.

squawks.headline: US retail sales rise 6.8% y/y in October, up from 6.29% in the previous month
squawks.detail: The annual figure was released with the October US retail sales report, which showed a 0.2% monthly rise. The previous month's annual rate was 6.29%.

squawks.headline: US import prices rise 1.1% m/m, above 0.7% forecast; export prices up 1.1% against 0.5% expected
squawks.detail: US import prices rose 1.1% m/m, matching the previous reading and above the 0.7% forecast. Export prices rose 1.1% m/m, against a 0.5% forecast and 2.2% previously.

squawks.headline: Canada's Carney and Mexico's Sheinbaum restate their commitment to renewing the USMCA trade agreement
squawks.detail: A joint statement says the Canadian Prime Minister and the Mexican President reaffirmed their commitment to renewing the Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement.

squawks.headline: US retail sales rise 0.2% m/m in October, above 0.1% forecast; core sales up 0.6% against 0.4% expected
squawks.detail: US headline retail sales grew 0.2% m/m, compared with a 0.1% forecast and 0.8% previously. Core retail sales rose 0.6% m/m, against a 0.4% forecast and 0.9% previously.

squawks.headline: Dollar returns to levels last seen in April 2025 on rising rate expectations; euro falls to 19-month low of $1.0982
squawks.detail: The FT reports that the US dollar has recovered all of its 'liberation day' losses as US rate expectations rise. LSEG data show the euro at a 19-month low of $1.0982.

squawks.headline: US ADP weekly employment change rises to 23.75K from 19.75K
squawks.detail: ADP's weekly private payrolls estimate came in at 23.75K, against 19.75K the previous week. No forecast was given.

squawks.headline: Destatis revises German October HICP up to 2.9% y/y from 2.8%
squawks.detail: The German statistics office also revised October CPI to -0.1% m/m from -0.2%.

squawks.headline: Fed's Musalem says monetary policy needs to respond immediately and AI is bringing forward demand and investment
squawks.detail: St Louis Fed President Musalem made the further remarks after earlier saying several rate hikes are likely needed before spring.

squawks.headline: Quad statement voices grave concern over economic coercion and arbitrary export restrictions, and pledges to secure supply chains
squawks.detail: A Quad joint statement opposes unilateral or coercive moves to change the status quo and commits to secure critical supply chains and protect freedom of navigation. It also announces closer cooperation on cybersecurity and affirms the AI accelerator.

squawks.headline: McFadden says the government will publish a white paper on its jobs settlement plans in the new year
squawks.detail: Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden said a white paper setting out the jobs settlement plans will be published in the new year. The announcement follows the Milburn welfare review, which put potential savings at £3.8bn a year by 2036.

squawks.headline: Work and Pensions Secretary McFadden says the PM and cabinet back the need for an entirely new system for young people
squawks.detail: UK Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden said the Prime Minister and cabinet have endorsed the need for a whole new system for young people. The remarks come as the Milburn welfare review is published.

squawks.headline: Fed's Musalem says several rate hikes are likely needed before spring and warns high inflation may persist
squawks.detail: St Louis Fed President Musalem said acting soon is the best way to ease price pressures without hurting jobs and growth, and that inflation is most likely to stay elevated unless the Fed raises rates. He also said bond yields would rise if the public doubted the Fed's resolve, and that he was optimistic above-trend GDP growth would continue.

squawks.headline: China's commerce ministry opposes US chip export curb and says it will take countermeasures if the US goes ahead
squawks.detail: China's commerce ministry said it strongly opposes the US move to curb chip exports and will respond with countermeasures if Washington insists on it.

squawks.headline: Trump signs trade deal with Thailand; Thailand to remove all tariffs on US exports
squawks.detail: Trump signed the deal with Thailand's Prime Minister on the sidelines of the ASEAN Summit. He said Thailand will remove all tariffs on US exports and substantial non-tariff barriers, including on US vehicles, with details to be finalised in the coming weeks.

squawks.headline: Houthis threaten Saudi interests and facilities in retaliation for Saudi strikes on Sana'a province
squawks.detail: Yemen's Houthis said Saudi attacks on Sana'a province and other provinces would be answered, and named Saudi interests and facilities as targets. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Hungary says it has an extension letting it import Russian oil without the risk of US sanctions
squawks.detail: Hungary's foreign ministry said on 17 November that it has received an extension that lets it keep importing Russian oil without exposure to US sanctions. The ministry did not give the length of the extension.

squawks.headline: Russian Deputy PM Novak orders oil refineries restored more quickly, reports say
squawks.detail: Reports say Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak has ordered work to restore the country's oil refineries to be speeded up. No timetable or volumes were given.

squawks.headline: Milburn says his youth employment plan will save only £200m a year, and not until 2036
squawks.detail: The Guardian reports that Alan Milburn, author of the welfare review, says most of the money saved from benefit cuts for young people will go towards funding a new job support system.

squawks.headline: Trump says the US is treating a possible Iranian threat to Washington very seriously
squawks.detail: US President Trump said the US is taking a possible Iranian threat to Washington very seriously. He had earlier warned Iran of an unprecedented response to any such threat. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Polish Prime Minister Tusk says Poland will freeze household gas prices
squawks.detail: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said the government will freeze gas prices for households. The report gave no further details on the level or duration of the freeze.

squawks.headline: Iran's foreign minister briefs the Sultan of Oman on an initiative to end the war
squawks.detail: Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi held talks on the region with the Sultan of Oman and briefed him on an initiative to end the war. He said Iran has always been serious about diplomacy.

squawks.headline: US administration presses ahead with plan to block imports of Chinese data centre equipment despite tech industry lobbying
squawks.detail: Reuters reports, citing people briefed on the matter, that the Trump administration is moving forward with the curb despite pushback from Amazon, Google, Meta and other US technology companies.

squawks.headline: Milburn says his welfare plan could cut the benefits bill before the next election, with full savings taking years
squawks.detail: Alan Milburn called for an overhaul of the welfare state ahead of publishing his youth unemployment report, the Guardian reports. He said the bill could fall before the next election but the overall savings would take years to arrive.

squawks.headline: BofA fund manager survey shows investors at their smallest bond underweight since November 2025
squawks.detail: The Bank of America fund manager survey shows investors at their smallest underweight in bonds since November 2025. A net 32% of respondents expect global CPI to be lower in 12 months.

squawks.headline: Trump says he will push Xi and Putin to help end the war in Ukraine
squawks.detail: US President Trump said he would press China's President Xi and Russia's President Putin to help bring the Ukraine war to an end. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Trump says a Russia-Ukraine deal is very close and he would meet Putin separately if possible
squawks.detail: US President Trump made the remarks on the sidelines of Quad talks with the leaders of Japan, India and Australia. He said he would hold a separate meeting with Putin if one could be arranged.

squawks.headline: Trump warns Iran of an unprecedented response to any threat on Washington; Tehran rejects CNN dirty bomb report
squawks.detail: US President Trump said the US takes the threat very seriously and that this is why Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon. Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson called a CNN report of a possible Iranian plan to set off a dirty bomb in Washington baseless.

squawks.headline: European Commission raises euro zone growth forecasts on AI-driven exports and halves its GDP projections for France
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that the Commission's latest forecasts raise the euro zone growth outlook as the AI boom lifts exports. The forecasts also show the bloc's largest economies diverging, with France's GDP projections halved.

squawks.headline: EU's Dombrovskis says second-round inflation effects are appearing in the economy
squawks.detail: European Commissioner Valdis Dombrovskis said second-round inflation effects are now being seen in the economy.

squawks.headline: Russia's Lavrov says Moscow would treat French troops deployed in Ukraine as direct participation in the war
squawks.detail: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said Moscow would regard any deployment of French soldiers in Ukraine as direct participation in the conflict.

squawks.headline: German 2-year Schatz auction clears at 3.1% with bid-to-cover of 1.8
squawks.detail: The German 2-year Schatz auction produced an average yield of 3.1%, up from 3.08% at the previous sale. The bid-to-cover ratio was 1.8, up from 1.3 last time.

squawks.headline: FT says Berlin's choice of Brunnermeier for the ECB board seals a deal with France for Spain's de Cos to lead the ECB
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that Germany's pick of Markus Brunnermeier as its ECB board nominee consolidates an agreement with France under which Pablo Hernández de Cos would become ECB president.

squawks.headline: Qatar says its mediation between the US and Iran is continuing
squawks.detail: Qatar said its efforts to mediate between the US and Iran are still under way. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: European Commission puts euro zone inflation at 3.2% in 2026, easing to 3.1% in 2027; GDP growth 1.2% in both years
squawks.detail: The European Commission's forecasts put euro zone inflation at 2.1% in 2028 and GDP growth at 1.3% that year. They show the aggregate budget deficit rising to 3.5% of GDP in 2026 from 3.0%, then to 3.8% by 2028, and public debt rising to 89.6% of GDP in 2026 and 91.3% by 2028.

squawks.headline: German ZEW economic sentiment rises to 35.6, beating 28.8 forecast; current conditions improve to -33.2
squawks.detail: The German ZEW economic sentiment index came in at 35.6, against a 28.8 forecast and 28.1 previously, while the current conditions index was -33.2, against a -35.3 forecast and -35.9 previously. The eurozone ZEW expectations index rose to 26.5 from 18.5.

squawks.headline: Germany to back Spain's de Cos for ECB president, sources say
squawks.detail: Two sources say Germany will support the Spanish candidate, Pablo Hernández de Cos, for the ECB presidency. This follows the German government's nomination of Markus Brunnermeier for the post of ECB chief economist.

squawks.headline: Iranian state media say a liquefied gas carrier and an oil tanker are on fire in the Strait of Hormuz after hitting naval mines
squawks.detail: Iranian state media, citing the Revolutionary Guards, report that both vessels caught fire after striking mines in the Strait of Hormuz. No market reaction is reported in the post.

squawks.headline: Iraq's oil minister puts initial Kirkuk-Ceyhan export capacity at 120,000 bpd, rising gradually to 500,000 bpd
squawks.detail: Iraq's oil minister says crude exports via the Iraq-Turkey pipeline will start at 120,000 barrels per day. He says capacity will be increased step by step until it reaches 500,000 barrels per day.

squawks.headline: Iraq's oil minister says crude exports through the Iraq-Turkey pipeline have resumed
squawks.detail: Iraq's oil minister said crude pumping for export has restarted via the Iraq-Turkey pipeline. No volumes were given.

squawks.headline: Zelenskiy confirms Ukraine's military struck Russia's Crimean bridge, calling it a response to strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure
squawks.detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskiy said the strike was the seventh stage of an operation run over several weeks by the SBU and the General Staff. He described it as retaliation for Russian attacks on Ukraine's infrastructure.

squawks.headline: German Chancellor backs proposing Brunnermeier for ECB chief economist post, government sources say
squawks.detail: Government sources say the German Chancellor supports the decision to put forward Markus Brunnermeier for the ECB role. The finance minister has already nominated him, and the cabinet is due to decide tomorrow.

squawks.headline: Italy's final CPI is revised up to 5.5% y/y from 5.4%; final HICP confirmed at 5.6%
squawks.detail: Italy's final October CPI rose 1% m/m against a 0.9% forecast, and annual CPI came in at 5.5% against a forecast of 5.4%. Final HICP matched expectations at 1.2% m/m and 5.6% y/y.

squawks.headline: Russia says no date is set for the next round of Ukraine talks and calls Ukraine joining NATO unacceptable
squawks.detail: Russian officials said no date has been fixed for the next round of Ukraine peace talks, according to Tass and other reports. Russia's foreign ministry, via Sergei Ryabkov, said Ukraine's entry into NATO is unacceptable to Moscow, Interfax reported.

squawks.headline: Russia says it has had no response yet to its security proposals
squawks.detail: Russia said it has not yet received any feedback on its security proposals, Interfax reported, as Ukraine peace talks continue.

squawks.headline: Russia says there is no understanding yet on continuing Ukraine peace talks
squawks.detail: Russia said there was no understanding yet on continuing the Ukraine talks, Interfax reported. The Kremlin had earlier said the next round of Russia-Ukraine-US talks had been agreed.

squawks.headline: Germany's finance minister nominates Markus Brunnermeier for ECB chief economist; cabinet to decide tomorrow
squawks.detail: The German Finance Ministry says the finance minister has put forward Markus Brunnermeier for the ECB chief economist post. It says the German cabinet is due to decide on the nomination tomorrow.

squawks.headline: UK Milburn welfare review puts potential savings at £3.8bn a year by 2036
squawks.detail: The Milburn welfare review estimates that its proposals could save £3.8bn a year by 2036. The review is due to propose cutting sickness benefits for under-25s and spending more on employment support.

squawks.headline: Japan proposes an 'Asian IEA' to manage joint regional oil stockpiles
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that Tokyo has proposed joint oil reserves for the region. The aim is to protect import-dependent Asian economies from future energy shocks.

squawks.headline: China pledges to protect its firms' rights and interests after the US moves to restrict remote access to AI chips
squawks.detail: China's foreign ministry spokesperson Guo responded to the US Commerce Department rule restricting remote access to advanced AI chips and tightening re-export controls. No specific countermeasures were reported.

squawks.headline: UK regular pay growth slows to 3.5% from 3.7%; October claimant count rises 33.2K, above 25.4K estimate
squawks.detail: ONS figures show average earnings excluding bonuses grew 3.5% in the three months to September, down from 3.7%, while employment rose 156K on the 3M/3M measure after 102K previously. The claimant count rose 33.2K in October, compared with 9.8K the month before and an estimate of 25.4K.

squawks.headline: UK unemployment rate falls to 4.6%, below 4.7% forecast; average weekly earnings growth eases to 3.6%
squawks.detail: UK labour market data show the unemployment rate at 4.6% (forecast and previous 4.7%), average weekly earnings growth at 3.6% year on year (forecast 3.5%, previous 3.7%) and 3m/3m employment up 155K (forecast 139K, previous 102K). Unemployment change came in at 33.2K (previous 30.3K), and seasonally adjusted employment change was -34K against a 10K forecast (previous 13K).

squawks.headline: China and Canada back putting a central bank currency swap into effect and open China's panda bond market to Canadian firms
squawks.detail: China's finance ministry said both sides support steps by the Bank of Canada and the People's Bank of China to bring a local currency swap deal into effect, and that qualified Canadian institutions may issue panda bonds on Chinese exchanges. The statement also says the two countries aim for trade results before their leaders meet at APEC.

squawks.headline: Finland's President Stubb urges European leaders to hold direct talks with Putin
squawks.detail: According to the Financial Times, Stubb said it was irresponsible for Europe to have left negotiations with Russia to the US.

squawks.headline: Oman and Iran foreign ministers discuss shipping security and reviving negotiation channels
squawks.detail: Oman's foreign ministry said the two foreign ministers discussed the security of shipping and maritime corridors, and ways to reactivate diplomatic channels and resume negotiations.

squawks.headline: Canada extends and widens its trade arrangement with China and adds tariff relief on about C$400 million of exports
squawks.detail: The Canadian Prime Minister's office says the relief includes $116 million of frozen pork exports and $285 million of fish and seafood shipments, and that Canada will keep remission measures on some Chinese steel and aluminium products for two more years. The announcement follows talks between Prime Minister Carney and President Xi before APEC.

squawks.headline: RBNZ survey puts New Zealand's average two-year inflation expectations at 2.36% for the fourth quarter
squawks.detail: The figure comes from the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's quarterly survey of expectations, released on 17 November.

squawks.headline: RBA minutes say inflation pressures will stay uncomfortably high for at least 12 more months and neutral rate has likely risen
squawks.detail: The Reserve Bank of Australia's minutes say domestic demand is likely to exceed capacity until the middle of 2027 and global developments have probably pushed the neutral rate higher. Members who backed a hike said 2026 tightening had not contained inflation, while those against it warned of a deeper contraction.

squawks.headline: RBA minutes show board weighed a 25bp rate hike against holding, with hike case based on a worsening inflation outlook
squawks.detail: The Reserve Bank of Australia minutes say members who favoured a hike judged earlier 2026 increases insufficient, while those against feared the economy was nearing a sharper downturn. Members said inflation risks remain skewed to the upside, excess demand is seen lasting until mid-2027, and global developments have probably lifted Australia's real neutral rate.

squawks.headline: RBA Governor Bullock says inflation risks are still skewed to the upside and oil prices may stay high
squawks.detail: Reserve Bank of Australia Governor Bullock said the risks to inflation remain tilted to the upside. She also pointed to the risk that oil prices stay elevated.

squawks.headline: UK Milburn welfare review to propose cutting sickness benefits for under-25s and spending billions on employment support
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that the review led by former minister Alan Milburn will set out a plan to reduce sickness benefits for under-25s while putting billions of pounds into employment support.

squawks.headline: UK Prime Minister Burnham says next steps on EU options will take time; ministers expect a timescale of months
squawks.detail: Burnham said in a speech that the work would take time. According to a political journalist, ministers expect the next steps in setting out the UK's options on the EU to take months rather than weeks.

squawks.headline: US Secretary of State Rubio condemns Iran's attacks on Bahrain and restates US commitment to Bahrain's security
squawks.detail: The State Department says Rubio made the remarks in a call with Bahrain's foreign minister.

squawks.headline: IMF reports significant progress with Ukraine on reviews of its loan programme and estimates a $32-34bn financing gap for 2027
squawks.detail: IMF staff say Ukraine's performance under the extended fund facility has improved since the first review, with virtual talks on the second and third reviews ongoing; they estimate a financing gap of $32-34 billion in 2027 and $17 billion in 2028. Given financing assurances, the review will go to the IMF board for approval, opening access to $1.6 billion.

squawks.headline: UK Prime Minister Burnham says the UK's options on the EU will shape decisions in the next Parliament
squawks.detail: Prime Minister Burnham said on 16 November that the UK's options on its relationship with the EU will feed into decisions taken in the next Parliament. He spoke ahead of this week's UK-EU summit.

squawks.headline: Fed's Hammack says she does not yet see a case for more aggressive rate hikes, despite worsening inflation pressures
squawks.detail: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack told Bloomberg TV on Monday that she still favours slow, steady rate increases, Reuters reports. She said inflation pressures have been getting worse rather than better.

squawks.headline: UK Prime Minister Burnham says Britain's exit from Europe left bad feeling on both sides
squawks.detail: Prime Minister Burnham commented on the UK's departure from Europe ahead of this week's UK-EU summit. The post did not report any new policy step.

squawks.headline: CFTC data show speculators extend US 2-year Treasury futures net short; sterling net short at 43,216 contracts
squawks.detail: In the week to 10 November, CFTC data show speculators added 110,201 contracts to their CBOT US 2-year Treasury futures net short, taking it to 1,112,745, and added 48,694 contracts to the 5-year net short, taking it to 1,324,064. The same data show a sterling net short of 43,216 contracts, a euro net short of 136,396 and a yen net long of 123,113.

squawks.headline: Iranian state media says a fourth tanker in 24 hours has hit a mine in the Strait of Hormuz
squawks.detail: Iran's state broadcaster IRIB reports that a fourth tanker has struck a mine in the Strait of Hormuz within 24 hours. The post gives no further details and reports no market reaction.

squawks.headline: RBNZ says domestic financial stress has eased from last year's peak but remains uneven; deposit takers well placed
squawks.detail: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand says sectors that depend on discretionary spending still face challenges, while deposit takers are well positioned to manage financial risks.

squawks.headline: RBNZ says global financial stability risks keep rising, citing higher bond yields and stretched AI valuations
squawks.detail: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand's Financial Stability Report says the financial system and deposit takers remain resilient. It also says higher government bond yields and stretched valuations, particularly among AI-related firms, leave markets vulnerable to a correction, and that domestic stress has eased from last year's peak but remains uneven.

squawks.headline: Brent crude futures settle 3.55% lower at $92.44 a barrel, down $3.40
squawks.detail: Brent futures closed Monday's session down $3.40, or 3.55%, at $92.44 a barrel. US crude futures had settled 3.21% lower earlier in the day.

squawks.headline: US crude futures settle 3.21% lower at $85.72 a barrel, down $2.84
squawks.detail: NYMEX WTI December crude futures settled at $85.72 a barrel on Monday, down $2.84 or 3.21%. December diesel futures settled at $4.0818 a gallon and December natural gas at $3.1220/MMBtu.

squawks.headline: US Vice President Vance says the US will not let Iran turn into even a two-year commitment
squawks.detail: US Vice President JD Vance made the remark in a Fox News clip. The inputs report no market reaction.

squawks.headline: Fed's Hammack wants policy to reach a restrictive stance and says financial conditions are not yet restraining the economy
squawks.detail: Cleveland Fed President Hammack said higher market borrowing costs are needed to restrain the economy, that the economy can cope with more restriction and that it is unclear how far the Fed must go. She also said AI is adding to inflation pressures now, that strong growth and Fed expectations are pushing rates higher, and that 2% remains a reasonable inflation goal.

squawks.headline: Fed's Hammack says she prefers slow, steady rate hikes in small steps and sees signs the labour market may be tightening
squawks.detail: Cleveland Fed President Hammack said she is concerned that businesses are more willing to accept price rises and are passing more of them on. She described the job market as broadly in balance but not dynamic, with possible early signs of tightening, and said the impact of AI could vary widely.

squawks.headline: Fed's Hammack says inflation pressures are broadening and bigger rate moves may be needed if an inflation mindset takes hold
squawks.detail: Cleveland Fed President Hammack said she prefers steady, smaller rate hikes and that inflation is moving in the wrong direction across more sectors, with businesses passing on price rises to protect margins. She said inflation expectations remain reasonably anchored and that she goes into every FOMC meeting with an open mind.

squawks.headline: US envoy Kushner says work has begun on the agenda for the next multilateral Ukraine peace meeting, which the US aims to hold soon
squawks.detail: Kushner said he and Witkoff spoke with Kremlin aide Ushakov on Monday about progress so far and next steps. He added that NATO will remain a critical pillar of European security and that both Russia and Ukraine must agree to any final peace deal.

squawks.headline: US envoy Kushner says Ukraine talks have made progress on security guarantees, a path to EU membership and a postwar security plan
squawks.detail: US envoy Jared Kushner said negotiations had advanced over the past year on core elements, including security guarantees for Ukraine and its route to EU membership. He added that any final peace agreement would require the consent of both Russia and Ukraine.

squawks.headline: US envoy Kushner says he and Witkoff discussed with Kremlin aide Ushakov how to enable direct talks between Europe and Russia
squawks.detail: US envoy Jared Kushner said on Monday that he and Steve Witkoff spoke with Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov about progress so far and the next steps in the Ukraine peace process, including how to facilitate direct engagement between Europe and Russia. Kushner also said NATO will remain a critical pillar of European security.

squawks.headline: Zelenskiy says leaders will meet in Berlin to agree negotiating steps after online talks with US envoys
squawks.detail: Ukraine's president said leaders will gather in Berlin to agree the next negotiating steps. He added that a new round of online discussions took place on Monday, with US envoys Witkoff and Kushner and European representatives taking part.

squawks.headline: Two-year gilt yield rises above 5% for the first time since 2023 as traders add bets on further BoE hikes
squawks.detail: City AM reports the two-year gilt yield rose 4bp on Monday to pass 5%. Investors are pricing three more Bank of England rate rises before April.

squawks.headline: Iran's army shoots down a US MQ-1 drone near the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian media report
squawks.detail: Iran's Mehr News Agency reports that Iranian army air defences downed an American MQ-1 drone close to the Strait of Hormuz. Separately, Mehr reports that air defence systems were activated in Isfahan minutes earlier; no market reaction is reported.

squawks.headline: Fed Chair Warsh says the AI boom could support markedly faster US growth without fuelling inflation
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that Fed Chair Warsh said AI-driven innovation could hold US GDP above its long-run average without adding to inflation.

squawks.headline: Fitch says the outlook for North American sovereigns is deteriorating as divided US government raises fiscal risks
squawks.detail: Fitch Ratings says divided US government and brinkmanship over the debt ceiling are adding to fiscal risks, and that Democrat majorities in both houses of Congress will likely bring more scrutiny of the administration's policies. It says improving growth and narrowing deficits support Canada's outlook for 2027, while trade tensions and tighter monetary policy weigh on it.

squawks.headline: Fed Chair Warsh says Fed staff have begun modelling superintelligence scenarios and flags risk from disappointing AI investment
squawks.detail: Fed Chair Warsh said a disappointment in AI investment could lead to an equity sell-off, an economic slowdown and higher unemployment. He described the AI scenarios as illustrative rather than forecasts.

squawks.headline: Fed Chair Warsh warns superintelligence could be highly disruptive and costly, with outcomes up to high unemployment
squawks.detail: In a speech, Fed Chair Warsh said the risks of superintelligence should not be overlooked. He said outcomes could range from widely shared gains to high unemployment, or to a slowdown caused by falling equity valuations if the technology disappoints.

squawks.headline: Fed Chair Warsh says superintelligence will have significant economic effects with implications for the Fed
squawks.detail: Fed Chair Warsh said the Fed must ask the right questions about new technologies and be ready for what follows, adding that the magnitude, scope and timing of the impact of superintelligence remain open questions. He also said humans should remain the decision-makers on how such technology is used; no remarks on the rate outlook were reported.

squawks.headline: US 3- and 6-month bill auctions clear at higher yields of 4.155% and 4.31%
squawks.detail: The US Treasury sold $95bn of 3-month bills at a high yield of 4.155% (previous 4.060%), with a bid-to-cover ratio of 2.76 (previous 2.670). It also sold $82bn of 6-month bills at 4.31% (previous 4.145%), with a bid-to-cover ratio of 2.83 (previous 2.920).

squawks.headline: Russia's Lavrov says many disputes remain in Moscow-Washington talks and dismisses Europe's past Ukraine mediation
squawks.detail: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said many points of disagreement remain in bilateral dialogue between Russia and the US. He also said Europe had repeatedly had chances to mediate on Ukraine and suggested those efforts had failed.

squawks.headline: EU's Kallas says a ceasefire must come before any talks with Russia on security architecture
squawks.detail: The EU's foreign policy chief said on Monday that a ceasefire in Ukraine must be in place before the bloc discusses security architecture with Russia. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: EU's Kallas says a 22nd Russia sanctions package will be presented in the coming days
squawks.detail: The EU foreign policy chief spoke after the foreign ministers' meeting. She said ministers had approved 140 new sanctions on Russia.

squawks.headline: EU's Kallas says the bloc is preparing further sanctions on Iran, citing cyberattacks in France
squawks.detail: The EU foreign policy chief said after the foreign ministers' meeting that further Iran sanctions are being prepared. She said cyberattacks in France show Europe is within Iran's reach.

squawks.headline: Supertanker rates fall more than 60% from October's record highs as geopolitical risk premium unwinds
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that the cost of shipping oil in the largest tankers has dropped sharply since the start of November. It attributes the fall to weaker chartering demand and the unwinding of the geopolitical risk premium that pushed rates to a record in October.

squawks.headline: US crude futures drop $2 as oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz show signs of recovering
squawks.detail: US crude futures fell $2 a barrel on Monday afternoon. Signs that oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz are recovering added to expectations of surplus supply.

squawks.headline: Bank of Canada Governor Macklem is to step down in June 2027 when his seven-year term ends
squawks.detail: The Bank of Canada said in a statement that Governor Tiff Macklem will leave his post in June 2027, at the end of his seven-year term.

squawks.headline: Kremlin says next round of Russia-Ukraine-US peace talks is agreed but denies agreeing to include Europeans
squawks.detail: A Kremlin aide said the next round of three-way Ukraine talks has been agreed, probably in Abu Dhabi again, with no date set yet, and that for now only Russia, Ukraine and the US are taking part. The aide contradicted US negotiators by saying Russia had not agreed to include Europeans, and said a lot must be settled before they could join, which could take more than one further round.

squawks.headline: Trump threatens heavy tariffs on Mexico unless it stops migrant caravans
squawks.detail: US President Trump said migrant caravans will not be allowed into the US and that he would impose heavy tariffs on Mexico if it does not stop them. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Trump says Ukraine is losing, and that Iran, Ukraine and trade will be on the agenda when he meets Xi and Putin in China
squawks.detail: US President Trump said his meeting with China's Xi and Russia's Putin in China would cover denuclearisation, Iran, Ukraine, the economy and trade. He also said Ukraine is losing and that Putin is backing down a little on Ukraine but could be tougher.

squawks.headline: Brent futures drop 2% to $93.92 a barrel as Middle East flows recover
squawks.detail: A market commentator reports that Brent crude futures fell 2% to $93.92 a barrel, attributing the decline to recovering oil flows from the Middle East.

squawks.headline: New York Fed's Nordstrom says FX markets are holding up well despite an uncertain global economy
squawks.detail: Julie Nordstrom, an official at the New York Fed, said foreign exchange markets have stayed resilient against an uncertain global economic backdrop. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Houthis take territory on Yemen's southern coast and move closer to Aden after government forces pull back
squawks.detail: Reuters, citing military sources, reported on Monday that Houthi fighters have seized ground on the southern coast after Saudi-backed government forces fell back to defend Aden.

squawks.headline: Kremlin says Putin-Trump-Xi joint statement is under negotiation ahead of the 19 November meeting, and that Putin will meet Trump
squawks.detail: The Kremlin said the three-way meeting will take place on 19 November at Xi's official residence. It expects a joint communique, and said Putin and Trump will hold separate talks that day, with format and venue still being finalised; Putin is also due to brief Xi on 18 November about his contacts with the US, including the Abu Dhabi talks.

squawks.headline: New York Fed's Empire State manufacturing index falls to 7.8 in November, well below the 18 forecast
squawks.detail: The New York Fed's Empire State manufacturing index fell to 7.8 in November from 25.5 in October, against a forecast of 18.

squawks.headline: Canada's core inflation measures are mixed in October: CPI-median at 2%, CPI-trim at 1.8%, CPI-common at 2.5%
squawks.detail: Canada's October CPI-median rose to 2% from 1.9%, as forecast, while CPI-trim held at 1.8% against a 1.9% forecast and CPI-common rose to 2.5% from 2.4%. Headline CPI was 3.1% on the year against a 3.2% forecast, and rose 0.2% on the month against a 0.3% forecast; the BoC core measure was 2.0% on the year, down from 2.2%.

squawks.headline: Canada's October CPI inflation comes in at 3.1%
squawks.detail: Canada's consumer price inflation for October was reported at 3.1%. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: US Commerce Department issues rule restricting remote access to advanced AI chips and tightening re-export controls
squawks.detail: The US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security published a rule restricting remote access to advanced AI chips. It also requires a licence to re-export them to Brazil and Singapore and publishes a list of countries it deems higher than normal risk.

squawks.headline: Several explosions reported in Riyadh after attacks from Yemen, Iran's Fars news agency says
squawks.detail: Iran's Fars news agency says explosions were heard in the Saudi capital following attacks launched from Yemen. This comes after Yemen's Houthis said they had attacked a pumping station on Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline.

squawks.headline: European Commission imposes anti-dumping duties on cold-rolled flat steel from India, Japan, Taiwan, Turkey and Vietnam
squawks.detail: The European Commission has imposed anti-dumping duties on some cold-rolled flat steel products imported from India, Japan, Taiwan, Turkey and Vietnam.

squawks.headline: Knot expected to withdraw from the ECB leadership race this week, Volkskrant reports
squawks.detail: Dutch newspaper Volkskrant reports that Klaas Knot is expected to drop out of the race for the ECB post this week.

squawks.headline: EU Council formally lists 12 individuals and 101 entities in Russia's banking, finance, energy and shadow fleet sectors
squawks.detail: The EU Council says it has sanctioned 12 individuals and 101 entities in Russia's banking, financial and energy sectors and in its shadow fleet. It says the aim is to further limit Russia's ability to fund the war.

squawks.headline: European Commission says it is ready to host Ukraine talks in Europe, including with Russian delegates
squawks.detail: A European Commission spokesperson said the EU is prepared to host Ukraine talks in Europe that would include Russian delegates. The statement follows the EU's agreement on which countries and institutions will represent Europe in the peace talks.

squawks.headline: EU Council sanctions 30 individuals and two entities over Russian disinformation and cyber activity
squawks.detail: The Council of the EU says the listings fall under its regime on Russian foreign information manipulation and malicious cyber activity. They include the pro-Russian hacker group NoName057, the Moscow-based PR firm Social Design Agency and Chay Bowes of RT International.

squawks.headline: EU pays out €1.71bn to Ukraine for drones, ammunition and air defence
squawks.detail: Reports say the EU has disbursed €1.71bn to Ukraine to fund drones, ammunition and air defence.

squawks.headline: Ukraine hits the Crimean Bridge in a record drone attack, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that Ukraine struck the Crimean Bridge. Russia's defence ministry said it intercepted or destroyed more drones in the past 24 hours than at any point since the war began.

squawks.headline: Fed's Barr warns AI could pose risks to trading, cybersecurity and consumer and investor protection
squawks.detail: Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr set out the risks on Monday, Reuters reports. His remarks follow a Fed report last week that showed a sharp rise in concern about AI risks to financial stability.

squawks.headline: EU antitrust regulators give UniCredit's takeover of Commerzbank unconditional approval
squawks.detail: EU competition regulators have cleared UniCredit's acquisition of Commerzbank without conditions.

squawks.headline: EU imposes new Russia sanctions on 145 individuals and entities, France's foreign minister says
squawks.detail: France's foreign minister Jean-Noël Barrot said the EU has imposed sanctions on 145 individuals and legal entities. Earlier on Monday, Ireland's foreign minister had put the package at 113 listings.

squawks.headline: Eurozone industrial production rises 0.2% on the month but falls 1.5% on the year, both short of forecasts
squawks.detail: Eurozone industrial output rose 0.2% on the month, against a 0.3% forecast and a previous -0.5%. On the year it fell 1.5%, against a forecast of -0.2% and a previous -1.1%.

squawks.headline: France's foreign minister says Russia will not be allowed to set the terms of European security architecture
squawks.detail: France's foreign minister Barrot said Russia would not be allowed to dictate the terms of Europe's security architecture. He spoke as European officials pushed back on Russian demands linked to Ukraine peace talks.

squawks.headline: UK average house price falls 1.8% in November to £364,270, a steeper drop than the usual November decline
squawks.detail: Property-portal figures reported by City AM show the average UK house price fell 1.8% to £364,270 in November, against a ten-year average November fall of 1.1%. The report links the drop to higher mortgage rates since the Iran war, which have pushed sellers to cut their price expectations.

squawks.headline: Kremlin says Brussels pledges to keep aiding Ukraine and pressuring Russia do not help the peace process
squawks.detail: The Kremlin said it still hopes to hear Europe's position, declined to comment on the idea of Ukraine giving up Donbas in exchange for NATO membership, and denied Estonia's sabotage accusations. It also said a drone attack on the Crimea bridge caused minor damage and traffic is still running.

squawks.headline: France's foreign minister says the EU's new Russia sanctions list includes a St Petersburg oil terminal and the CEO of Wildberries
squawks.detail: French Foreign Minister Barrot named the St Petersburg oil terminal and the chief executive of Russian retailer Wildberries among the additions to the EU sanctions list. He also said France and the UK will host a conference in December on tackling Russia's shadow fleet.

squawks.headline: EU Council approves ninth Ukraine Facility payment of €8bn to Kyiv, the largest single payment under the Facility
squawks.detail: The EU Council approved the €8bn disbursement to Ukraine, which it described as the largest single payment under the Ukraine Facility since mid-2024.

squawks.headline: ECB's Vujcic sees no reason to change course on rates and says market pricing of another hike in 2027 looks reasonable
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member Boris Vujcic said there was no reason to change the direction of travel on rates. He added that markets pricing a further rate rise in 2027 did not seem unreasonable.

squawks.headline: UK and EU are set to announce food deals and a defence commitment at this week's summit, Reuters reports
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that Britain and the EU will use a summit this week to set out deals on food and a commitment on defence. The report describes these as a step towards the closer relationship sought by Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

squawks.headline: ECB's Vujcic says private-credit risks appear contained but need watching, and names valuations, funding and cyberattacks as AI risks
squawks.detail: ECB Vice-President Vujcic listed valuations, funding and cyberattacks among the risks linked to AI and said private-credit risks look contained but need monitoring. In the same remarks he repeated that recent moves in energy prices may add to inflation.

squawks.headline: ECB's Vujcic calls financial stability risks elevated, citing AI and sovereign debt, and says energy prices may push inflation higher
squawks.detail: ECB policymaker Vujcic says AI and high debts are the leading risks to financial stability, while private-credit risks look contained but need monitoring. He says wages are not responding materially to inflation, recent energy price moves may lift inflation, weaker confidence and higher borrowing costs should partly contain it, and Europe's economy is very resilient.

squawks.headline: Sweden's foreign minister says Russia is still not serious about Ukraine peace talks, pointing to its demands
squawks.detail: Sweden's foreign minister said Russia is still not engaging seriously on peace in Ukraine and called the demands it is now making absurd. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Lithuania's foreign minister says a ceasefire must come before any talks with Russia on European security architecture
squawks.detail: Lithuania's foreign minister said that discussing European security architecture with Russia now would be a trap and that a ceasefire in Ukraine is needed first. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: EU foreign ministers to agree a new package of Russia sanctions today with 113 listings, Ireland's foreign minister says
squawks.detail: Ireland's foreign minister says EU foreign ministers will agree a new Russia sanctions package on Monday, and that it will include 113 listings.

squawks.headline: China calls this week's trilateral meeting of the Chinese, US and Russian leaders groundbreaking
squawks.detail: China's Foreign Ministry said on Monday that this week's meeting between Xi, Trump and Putin is of groundbreaking significance and will support world peace and stability, Reuters reports.

squawks.headline: EU's Kallas calls Russian demands a pretext to keep the war going and says talks must now turn to substance
squawks.detail: The EU foreign policy chief said European leaders have settled the format for talks with Russia on Ukraine and must now discuss substance. She described Russia's demands as a clear pretext to continue the war.

squawks.headline: Yemeni government forces pull back from area near Bab el-Mandeb Strait to defend Aden
squawks.detail: Yemen's government forces say they are withdrawing from the area near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to concentrate on defending their main base in Aden. Reuters describes this as a major setback for the Saudi-backed campaign against the Iran-aligned Houthis.

squawks.headline: UK weighs scrapping post-Brexit border inspection sites ahead of trade reset with the EU, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that the UK government is considering closing border inspection sites built after Brexit as it prepares to reset trade relations with the EU.

squawks.headline: European Commission to propose a €45bn Ukraine loan backed by the EU budget, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that Brussels plans to put forward a €45bn loan for Ukraine, secured against the EU budget.

squawks.headline: Sterling falls to a one-month low against the US dollar, its weakest level since 15 October
squawks.detail: A market commentator reported that the pound had fallen to its weakest level against the dollar since 15 October. A separate FX report described the dollar as broadly firm.

squawks.headline: BoJ's Takata says rate rises are needed now and the BoJ should not be bound by market-priced hike intervals
squawks.detail: Takata, a BoJ board member, said the policy rate has nearly reached the neutral zone, that the bank should move flexibly in either direction based on data, and that rate rises abroad could lift Japan's neutral rate above market expectations. He also said funding conditions in Japan remain accommodative and the risk of a marked slowdown has eased.

squawks.headline: BoJ's Takata says price rises are now more likely to cause second-round effects
squawks.detail: Bank of Japan board member Takata also said that monitoring price developments passed through markets is essential, because some currency market participants are focusing on real and nominal interest rate differentials.

squawks.headline: China's October retail sales rise 0.4% and industrial output 4.8% on the year, both below forecasts
squawks.detail: Retail sales growth missed the 0.8% forecast, industrial output missed the 5.3% poll, and fixed-asset investment fell 8.1% in January to October against an expected 7.0% drop. Property investment fell 21.6% and the surveyed jobless rate was 5.1%, against a 5.2% forecast; USD/CNH was near flat after the data.

squawks.headline: Estonia will close all border crossings to Russia on 1 December after blaming the GRU for an attempted explosion
squawks.detail: Estonia's government said it would shut the crossings after accusing Russian military intelligence of being behind a failed explosion on Saturday at an Estonian drone maker, the FT reports.

squawks.headline: JGB yields rise across the curve, with the 30-year at 4.025% and the 20-year at 3.755%
squawks.detail: The 30-year JGB yield is up 2.5bp at 4.025% and the 20-year up 2bp at 3.755%. The 5-year is up 1bp at 2.26% and the 2-year up half a basis point at 1.88%.

squawks.headline: Japan's Q3 GDP deflator rises 2.4% on the year, below the 2.7% forecast
squawks.detail: Japan's economy minister Kiuchi says rising prices linked to Middle East tensions, natural disasters and poor weather hurt private consumption. He adds that better jobs and incomes should support a gradual recovery and that the impact of the Middle East situation needs close monitoring.

squawks.headline: US 10-year Treasury yield holds above 5% as traders await Fed minutes and more policymaker remarks
squawks.detail: A market report says rising Treasury yields, with the 10-year above 5%, weighed on gold, which steadied near $3,890 an ounce after a 4.6% fall last week. The report links the moves to strong US inflation data and hawkish Fed comments.

squawks.headline: Japan's Q3 GDP is flat on the quarter, short of the 0.1% forecast, and shrinks 0.1% annualised
squawks.detail: Preliminary July–September data show GDP at 0.0% quarter on quarter, against a forecast of 0.1% and 0.4% in the previous quarter. Annualised GDP fell 0.1%, against a poll of +0.3%. Private consumption fell 0.3%, capex rose 1.6% and the GDP deflator rose 2.4% year on year, below the 2.7% forecast. The dollar was reported steady at 159.72 yen after the release.

squawks.headline: Fed's Schmid says the Fed has work to do on inflation, with price pressures running too hot
squawks.detail: Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid said on Sunday that the Fed has the tools and the responsibility to deal with inflation. He added that it is not the Fed's job to influence the price of any single good or service.

squawks.headline: UK PM Burnham is set to address the costs of Brexit and push a reset with the EU ahead of a Brussels summit
squawks.detail: Prime Minister Andy Burnham is due to tell a City of London audience on Monday that he is ready for a national discussion about a longer-term agreement with Europe, ahead of a summit in Brussels this week. Briefings indicate he will restate the 2024 red lines.

squawks.headline: S&P affirms Italy's BBB+/A-2 sovereign ratings and keeps a positive outlook
squawks.detail: S&P Global Ratings affirmed Italy's long- and short-term sovereign ratings at BBB+/A-2 on Friday evening. The outlook stays positive.

squawks.headline: Fed financial stability report names AI as top risk; fiscal debt sustainability climbs to fifth, with warnings on disorderly yield rises
squawks.detail: Several respondents warned that persistent deficits and heavy Treasury issuance could cause a disorderly rise in yields; the report also put hedge fund leverage at its highest since 2013 and said advanced computing-related debt issuance had passed $680bn by October 2026, 31% of non-financial investment-grade corporate issuance.

squawks.headline: US Treasury says the government was $694.1bn below the $41.1tn debt limit as of 12 November
squawks.detail: The figure comes from US Treasury data and is as of 12 November.

squawks.headline: EU's Kallas says Russian demands for talks on European security architecture risk diverting focus from a Ukraine ceasefire
squawks.detail: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas made the remarks as the EU agreed on a group of five nations to represent Europe at Ukraine peace talks, Reuters reports.

squawks.headline: Yemen's Houthis say they attacked a pumping station on Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline
squawks.detail: Yemen's Houthis say they attacked a pumping station on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline. No details of damage or market reaction were reported in the inputs.

squawks.headline: Iran's IRGC Navy says two tankers struck sea mines and caught fire near the Strait of Hormuz
squawks.detail: Iranian media report that the IRGC Navy says two tankers hit sea mines near Hormuz and caught fire. No market reaction was reported in the inputs.

squawks.headline: New York Fed plans about $14bn of bill purchases for MBS reinvestment and extends pause on reserve management purchases
squawks.detail: The New York Fed desk plans about $14.0bn of reinvestment purchases and no reserve management purchases between 16 November and 11 December. This extends the pause on reserve management purchases to mid-December.

squawks.headline: Fed's Logan says the US Treasury market is working well despite rate volatility but the Fed should bolster its support tools
squawks.detail: Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan said on Friday that banks have improved their access to contingent funding over the past three years. She also said the Fed should strengthen its support tools for both the Treasury market and bank funding, Reuters reported.

squawks.headline: Market commentators flag suspected intervention in the yen
squawks.detail: A market commentary account reported suspected intervention in the yen late on Friday. It gave no figures and did not name an official source.

squawks.headline: EU's Costa says having several people on Europe's Ukraine negotiating team is normal
squawks.detail: European Council President Costa commented on Europe's delegation for the Ukraine peace talks. The EU institutions and five countries are due to represent Europe.

squawks.headline: US holds first official US-China Board of Trade meeting
squawks.detail: The US Trade Representative and the Treasury held the first official meeting of the US-China Board of Trade, according to a statement.

squawks.headline: Trump extends shipping waiver for oil and fertiliser by 90 days, White House official says
squawks.detail: A White House official said President Trump has extended a shipping waiver covering oil and fertiliser for 90 days.

squawks.headline: Fed's Daly says she is starting to hear the US consumer may be losing steam
squawks.detail: San Francisco Fed President Daly said businesses are cautiously optimistic but all are worried about inflation, and that there are early signs US consumers may be tiring.

squawks.headline: Von der Leyen says the EU will soon propose a 22nd package of sanctions on Russia
squawks.detail: European Commission President von der Leyen said a 22nd Russia sanctions package will be proposed soon. She also said the path to peace in Ukraine will not be easy, and that a European team of the E5 and EU institutions has been agreed for the talks.

squawks.headline: EU's von der Leyen says ending the war must be the focus and the EU will keep supporting Ukraine after it ends
squawks.detail: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the EU will support Ukraine while maintaining its own interests, and that ending the war must be the priority. She spoke on Friday evening, alongside separate remarks from EU Council President Costa that Ukraine's financial needs will be discussed at the next EU Council.

squawks.headline: Fed's Daly says services inflation excluding housing is not moving in the right direction
squawks.detail: San Francisco Fed President Daly said she is watching services inflation excluding housing closely. She also said the FOMC must be transparent, accountable and clear.

squawks.headline: EU's Costa confirms EU institutions and E5 will negotiate for Europe on Ukraine; next summit to discuss Ukraine's financing
squawks.detail: European Council President Costa said leaders agreed that the EU institutions plus Germany, France, Italy, Poland and the UK will form Europe's team in Ukraine peace talks. He added that the next EU Council will discuss Ukraine's financing needs for next year and beyond.
